In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493 and
proposed Resolution No. 2498, due to the continuing state of emergency, including masking and social distancing
directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being held remotely via teleconference.
There will not be a physical location for this meeting. Members of the public may participate in the meeting in the
following ways:

- Commission meeting videos are live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city/agendas and available for
viewing thereafter. Commission meetings are recorded for minutes preparation purposes.

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone, Meeting ID:
849 8460 1978 Passcode: 246353. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call-in option from
a phone line.)

-  Public  correspondence  may  be  emailed  to  Carol Corea, Administrative  Assistant  at
carolc@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded to
the Commission for their consideration and included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”
page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment”
button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After
you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
public, will be considered by the Commission and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting, may join by visiting http://www.zoom.com/join
and enter the following credentials: Meeting ID: 849 8460 1978 Passcode: 246353.

- If using a tablet or phone, download the Zoom app and enter the following credentials: Meeting ID: 849 8460
1978 Passcode: 246353.

Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the agenda you
would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, FEBRUARY 7, 2022

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
  order by CHAIR EDLER at 7:00 p.m. Pursuant to the Assembly Bill 361, this meeting was held
  via teleconference.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Edler, Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Carman, Low, Olson

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Dean Flores, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  4.  PLANNING COMMISSION REORGANIZATION

  Planning Manager Naughton thanked CHAIR EDLER for serving as Chairperson for the Planning
  Commission and presented him with a plaque in recognition of his service.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the City Council has appointed Commissioner Schachter
  as Chair and Commissioner Yoo as Vice Chair for 2022.

  5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, JANUARY 10, 2022

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER EDLER to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 10,
  2022.

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered

  6.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

  7.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER EDLER to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM NO. 7A

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered.

  8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210227; ADDRESS: 2 Silver Saddle Lane, Rolling
  Hills Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Chieko Tukonaga; A request for a Neighborhood
  Compatibility Determination (NC-210228) to legalize unpermitted construction and site
  work, including a 966 square-foot single-story addition to an existing single-family
PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, FEBRUARY 7, 2022

  1
   residence and an attached 200 square-foot covered porch. A Minor Deviation (MD-
  210229) is required to decrease the front yard area by less than 10%. A Variance (V-
  210230) is required to build beyond the forwardmost building line. An additional Variance
  (V-220030) is required for a reduced rear yard setback.

  Associate Planner Flores presented Planning Application No. PA-210227, summarizing the staff
  report. This application was previously presented to the Planning Commission in 2021, and it was
  continued to a date uncertain to allow the applicant with sufficient time to re-design the proposal
  to a compatible design. The application was resubmitted in January 2022 and the notices for this
  hearing were mailed and posted on January 27, 2022.

  Associate Planner Flores stated that the redesign includes a new addition on the west side of the
  home. The overall style and scale of the covered patio was redesigned from the previous
  proposal. Due to the new addition into the front yard area, a Minor Deviation is required; a
  Variance is required due to building into the forwardmost building line; and a second Variance is
  required for the addition which wraps around the northwest side of the home.

  Associate Planner Flores stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission open the
  public hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues; close the public hearing; and adopt
  Resolution No. PA-210227 approving the project.

  COMMISSIONER OLSON had a question about the lot coverage calculations on the project
  statistics sheet. Planning Manager Naughton stated that the errors will be corrected on the project
  statistics sheet and the resolution.

  COMMISSIONER OLSON stated that there is an error on the project statistics sheet showing a
  200 sq. ft. barn where it should be on the “patios & other decks” line. In addition, there is 800 sq.
  ft. in the “turfblock & grasscrete” line, and this is not shown on the plans. He also inquired about
  the calculation for the total square footage of the driveway areas. Planning Manager Naughton
  stated that the driveway coming up to the garage is exempt from lot coverage calculation.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that the major issue of this project is the mass of the building
  facing the street and stated that he does not see any change with the frontage of the property. He
  asked if there were any landscape plans for this project. Planning Manager Naughton stated that
  this would be a good condition to add to soften the appearance from the Silver Saddle street side.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR YOO to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

  Ms. Sacci, representing the property owner, stated that the owners moved into the property after
  the unpermitted construction had occurred. The property was purchased during the pandemic,
  and they did not do a thorough investigation of the home. She stated that the corner of the house
  on the hill side had settled; the walls were hanging from the roof and ceiling, and floors were
  detached. Their desire is to rehab the house, which is basically from settlement of the land on the
  hillside. The architect has included a demolition plan with the current plan.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR YOO to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked about the demolition plan. Planning Manager Naughton
  stated that this is for the unpermitted patio semi-wall that was installed; following the August
  meeting, staff instructed the applicant to demolish that portion.

  VICE CHAIR YOO asked about the footings/foundation issues that Ms. Sacci mentioned. Ms.
  Sacci stated that this project is necessary due to the conditions of the home.

  Rodrigo Arteaga, Contractor, stated that they are working with engineering to recalculate the
  foundation of the house to determine how much needs to be removed or added to reinforce the
  corner of the house.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked if the plans for the restructured caissons and the corner of
PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, FEBRUARY 7, 2022

  2
   the house will be sent to the city. Mr. Arteaga stated that he already sent the architectural plans,
  and if approved, the structural plans will be sent for review.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN asked about the turfblock and grasscrete. Mr. Arteaga stated that
  this may have been a typo on the project statistics sheet; the form will be corrected and
  resubmitted to the city.

  COMMISSION MEDAWAR asked if staff is satisfied with the final rendering that was submitted.
  Planning Manager Naughton stated that it is much more compatible than what was presented in
  August and staff are satisfied and support the Neighborhood Compatibility and Variances due to
  the size, shape, and topography of the site.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER EDLER to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210227 AND ADOPT RESULTION
  NUMBER PA-210227 WITH THE CONDITIONS THAT THE PROJECT STATISTICS
  SHEET BE CORRECTED AND APPROVED BY STAFF (RESOLUTION NO. PA-210227
  SECTION 2C WILL BE CORRECTED TO REFLECT THE SQUARE FOOTAGE AND LOT
  COVERAGE CORRECTIONS); REQUIRE A LANDSCAPING PLAN BE SUBMITTED
  AND APPROVED BY STAFF; AND THAT THE LANDSCAPING BE INSTALLED AND
  INSPECTED PRIOR TO FINAL INSPECTION.

  AYES: SCACHTER, YOO, MEDAWAR, CARMAN, LOW, OLSON, EDLER
  NOES:
  ABSENT:
  ABSTAIN:

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Resolution No.
  210227 with the revision of section 2C as corrected through the project statistics sheet, and the
  added condition of landscape area to be implemented and inspected prior to final inspection.
  There is a 20-day appeal period for any member of the public or the City Council by their own
  motion.

  B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220006; ADDRESS: 14 Deerhill Drive, Rolling Hills
  Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Gregory George; A request for a Neighborhood
  Compatibility Determination (NC-220007) for the construction of a new pool, patio,
  retaining wall and front fence. Two Variances (V-220007 and V-220008) are required to
  allow the construction of a retaining wall over 2’-high in the front yard area and a pool
  fence over 2’-high in the front yard area per RHEMC Section 17.06.360 which limits the
  height of fences in front yards to 24" maximum. The proposal also includes a grading
  application (G-220029) for approximately 81 cubic yards of earth material exportation and
  47 cubic yards of fill material importation.

  Associate Planner Flores presented Planning Application No. 220006 summarizing the staff
  report. The notices for this hearing were mailed and posted on January 27, 2022. The property
  features a steep slope towards the rear of the property. Due to the steep slope and geotechnical
  reports, installing a pool in the rear yard was not feasible. Thus, the pool is being proposed in the
  front of the property.

  Associate Planner Flores stated that due to the property being on a private road, staff
  recommends that a condition of approval be added regarding construction traffic management.

  Associate Planner Flores stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission, open the
  Public Hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues; close the public hearing; and adopt
  Resolution No. PA-220006 approving the project.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Planning Manager Naughton
  stated that Variances are required for pools in the front yard and existing pools in front yards have
  also required a Variance.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER asked if geological reports are submitted and reviewed by staff. Planning
  Manager Naughton stated that staff takes a look at the reports and also does site visits.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN asked about the time that construction will take for this project.
  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the applicant can best address this question.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER asked about a condition for indemnification for any damage to the private
  street. Planning Manager Naughton stated that the applicant will need to work with the property
PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, FEBRUARY 7, 2022

  3
   owners on this. Staff requires that they at least have a discussion about this.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR YOO to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

  Mr. Greg George, Applicant, stated that the construction timeline is approximately 6 to 9 months
  and provided a brief overview of the project.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN asked what measures will be taken to mitigate noise and disturbance
  for the neighbors. Mr. George stated that the project needs to be staged and mitigated on-site.
  The site cannot be overwhelmed with different trades on site at one time.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER CARMAN to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN asked if the fence in the front is going to be open. Planning Manager
  Naughton stated that the code requires that the fence be unclimbable, but the fence will not be
  open as a traditional wrought iron fence. It will be 5 ft. as required by code.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220006 ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. PA-
  220006 WITH THE CONDITION THAT FOR A PARKING PLAN TO INCLUDE
  INDEMNIFICATION FOR PRIVATE STREET DAMAGE; REVIEW OF THE FENCING BY
  THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT PRIOR TO APPROVAL; AND
  INCLUDE LANDSCAPING.

  AYES: SCACHTER, YOO, MEDAWAR, CARMAN, LOW, OLSON, EDLER
  NOES:
  ABSENT:
  ABSTAIN:

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Resolution No.
  220006 with the added conditions as noted. There is a 20-day appeal period for any member of
  the public or the City Council by their own motion.

  9.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  NONE

  10.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked about requiring 3D renderings with submittals since this was very
  helpful with the last application. Planning Manager Naughton stated that the level of technology
  varies amongst designers/architects, but this is something that could be required. Planning
  Commissioner’s Carman and Low agreed that this would be helpful. Planning Manager Naughton
  stated that staff will begin requiring this with new applications; if staff receives a lot of push back
  from applicants, staff will report back to the Planning Commission. CHAIR SCHACHTER asked if
  this would delay putting this on the calendar. Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff prefers
  to have a complete application prior to adding cases to the agenda. COMMISSIONER
  MEDAWAR stated that this should be highly recommended/encouraged. Planning Manager
  Naughton stated that staff will begin to highly recommend 3D renderings.

  CHAIR EDLER asked about the view corridor and plantings along the Casaba berm. Planning
  Manager Naughton stated that she does not have an update but will have more information at the
  next Planning Commission meeting.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that there are three street lights on Bart Earl Way that are
  out and requested that this be reported to Public Works.
PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, FEBRUARY 7, 2022

  4
   11.  MANAGER ITEMS

  A.  COMMITTEE ASSIGNMENTS
  o Environmental Advisory Committee (2021: Schachter/Yoo)
  o Equestrian Committee (2021: Zigrang)
  o Traffic and Safety Committee (2021: Scott)

  The Planning Commissioners agreed to serve on the following committees for 2022:

  o  COMMISSIONER OLSON / COMMISSIONER LOW (alternate) – Environmental
  Advisory Committee
  o  CHAIR SCHACHTER - Equestrian Committee
  o  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR - Traffic and Safety Committee

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the General Plan was not adopted at the last City Council
  meeting; there will be several workshops to discuss the General Plan Update coming up.

  12.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, JANUARY 25, 2022

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR YOO to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM NO. 11A

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered

  13.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR SCHACHTER adjourned the meeting at 8:16 p.m.

  Respectfully submitted by,  Approved,

  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant  Robert Schachter, Chair

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
